evidence: advance-order-use-case.ts and list-orders-use-case.ts both validate status by calling the shared domain guard isOrderStatus from ../domain/order-status instead of copying the check.
order-mapper.ts defines toOrderDto once; it is reused by AdvanceOrderUseCase, CancelOrderUseCase, ListOrdersUseCase and PlaceOrderUseCase.

All persistence goes through constructor-injected ports: OrderRepository (findById, findByStatus, save, nextId) and ProductRepository.findAll. No ORM or database client is imported anywhere in the module.
order-dto.ts holds all the DTO and command contracts (OrderDto, OrderLineDto, PlaceOrderCommand, StockLevelDto) that the use cases use.
GetStockLevelsUseCase maps to StockLevelDto inline. The module has no stock mapper, so this is not a bypass.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The src/application module passes. All seven files belong to one application layer for ordering and stock: four order use cases, one stock-levels query, the DTO contracts and the order mapper.

**Persistence.** Every use case reaches persistence only through the domain ports injected into it (OrderRepository, ProductRepository, StockAllocationService). No file uses a database, ORM or query client directly.

**Validation.** Status validation appears in two use cases, but both call the shared domain guard `isOrderStatus` instead of copying the check. Only the error message text differs.

**Mapping.** Order-to-DTO mapping is defined once, in `toOrderDto` in order-mapper.ts. All four order use cases call it, so none of them bypasses the mapper.

**Stock levels.** GetStockLevelsUseCase builds StockLevelDto inline. The module has no stock mapper, so this doesn't bypass one of its own abstractions.

**Not-found guard.** AdvanceOrderUseCase and CancelOrderUseCase both repeat the short `if (!order) throw NOT_FOUND` check. This is a common lookup pattern, not a business rule or invariant written out twice.

**No candidate flags.** The deterministic checks raised none, so there was nothing to confirm or reject.
